AI Quick Read The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation's (EPFO) proposed systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) could benefit retiring subscribers who want a regular income from their provident fund savings without having to withdraw the entire accumulated corpus at once. The facility will allow eligible members to receive their retirement savings in monthly, quarterly or half-yearly instalments, while the remaining balance continues to earn returns. The Central Board of Trustees (CBT), EPFO's apex decision-making body, approved the proposal at its 240th meeting chaired by Union Labour and Employment Minister Mansukh Mandaviya on 19 November 2026. The facility will be voluntary, giving retiring employees the flexibility to choose between a lump-sum withdrawal and periodic payouts. Who stands to benefit from EPFO's SWP facility? Around 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years with provident fund accumulations exceeding ₹ 5 lakh are expected to be the primary beneficiaries in the initial phase, according to the Labour Ministry. The facility is also expected to benefit future retirees who want to draw a regular income from their EPF savings instead of receiving the entire amount in one go. This could be particularly useful for employees who do not have a substantial pension or another dependable source of income after retirement. Rather than moving their entire EPF corpus into a bank deposit or another investment immediately after retirement , they can retain the unwithdrawn amount in the provident fund and receive periodic payouts. The plan could also help retirees who are concerned about reinvestment risks. When a large retirement corpus is withdrawn at once, individuals must decide where to invest it and how much to withdraw every month. A systematic withdrawal facility could make this process more structured. How will the EPFO systematic withdrawal plan work? Under the SWP framework, retiring members will be able to withdraw their EPF savings at regular intervals instead of taking the entire accumulated balance as a lump sum. The withdrawal frequency can be monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, depending on the member's preference. The remaining corpus will continue to stay invested in the EPF fund and earn interest at the applicable rate. This means subscribers can access a portion of their retirement savings while retaining ownership of the balance. The facility will be voluntary. Members who prefer to withdraw their entire eligible EPF corpus at retirement will not be compelled to opt for periodic withdrawals. The proposal also provides for protecting the interests of family members. If a subscriber dies during the withdrawal period, the nominee or dependent will be able to withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments, according to the Labour Ministry. Will the SWP replace the monthly EPF pension? No. The proposed SWP is different from the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS), under which eligible subscribers receive a monthly pension after completing at least 10 years of eligible service . The SWP will allow members to draw down their accumulated EPF savings periodically. It is intended to supplement retirement income rather than replace the monthly EPS pension. For retirees who qualify for both benefits, the two could provide separate sources of post-retirement income: a monthly EPS pension and periodic withdrawals from their EPF corpus. What happens to the remaining EPF balance if the subscriber dies? The proposal also provides for nominee and dependent rights. If a member dies while receiving SWP payouts, eligible family members will have the option to withdraw the remaining EPF balance or continue receiving periodic payments. This provision could offer greater financial flexibility to families that depend on the retiree's accumulated provident fund savings. However, the detailed operational framework, including the implementation process and other applicable conditions, will depend on the necessary amendments and notifications. The Labour Ministry said the corresponding amendments to the EPF Scheme would be notified after approval. It is also taking up a corresponding amendment to the Income-tax Act with the Finance Ministry. EPFO's SWP facility could help retirees manage their accumulated savings more systematically, particularly those who need regular income but do not want to surrender their entire retirement corpus at once. Its actual usefulness will depend on the withdrawal limits, payout structure and implementation rules.
